Genetics: own alleles (peacock, tiger, black bar and japan blue on the Y chromosome, swords, orange or yellow tails); crosses with guppies, the young are hybrids.
Catch: aquarium net in rivers, jungle water, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.forktail_rainbo:
Forktail Rainbowfish (Pseudomugil furcatus) from the rainforest streams of Papua New Guinea.
Small, blue-silver with big eyes; the male has yellow fin edges and yellow tips on the forked tail.
In a shoal of 6 or more, 23–28 °C, water: average. Counts 0.4 fish in the stocking.
Swims at the surface, peaceful. Spawns every day a few eggs into moss or a spawning mop.
Catch: aquarium net in jungle water and rivers, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.garra_rufa:
Garra (Garra rufa) from the rivers and warm springs of the Middle East; the "doctor fish" of fish spas.
Grey-brown with a darker stripe, a sucker disc under the mouth to hold on in fast water.
In a group of 5 or more, 18–32 °C, water: sensitive (likes oxygen). Counts 1 fish in the stocking.
Grazes algae from stones, glass and decoration. Egg scatterer.
Catch: aquarium net in rivers, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.glowlight_tetra:
Glowlight Tetra (Hemigrammus erythrozonus) from the Essequibo river in Guyana.
Translucent with a glowing orange-red line from snout to tail.
Shoal of 6 or more, 23–28 °C, water: sensitive. Counts 0.35 fish in the stocking.
Scatters its eggs (fine plants, spawning mop).
Catch: aquarium net in jungle water, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.green_chromis:
Green Chromis (Chromis viridis), a damselfish of the Indo-Pacific reefs.
Pale blue-green, swims in shoals above the corals.
Shoal of 5 or more, 24–28 °C, sea water (28–40 ‰). Counts 0.5 fish in the stocking.
Does not breed in a tank.
Catch: aquarium net in warm and lukewarm oceans, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.green_gold_cory:
Green Gold Cory (Corydoras melanotaenia) from the Rio Meta region in Colombia.
Gold-green with a dark side stripe and yellow-orange fins.
Shoal of 6 or more, 22–27 °C, water: sensitive. Counts 0.55 fish in the stocking.
Glues its eggs to the glass (after a cool water change).
Catch: aquarium net in rivers, jungle water, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.green_neon_tetr:
Green Neon Tetra (Paracheirodon simulans), also sold as Blue Neon, from the blackwater of the upper Rio Negro and Orinoco (Brazil, Colombia, Venezuela).
Smaller than the neon; the stripe runs over almost the whole body, green or (Blue Neon) blue, with hardly any red. Blue is recessive.
Shoal of 6 or more, 24–30 °C, water: very sensitive. Counts 0.25 fish in the stocking.
Scatters its eggs (fine plants, spawning mop).
Catch: aquarium net in jungle water, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.green_spotted_p:
Green Spotted Puffer (Tetraodon nigroviridis) from the mangroves and estuaries of South-East Asia.
Bright green with round black spots and a white belly; gets big and lives in brackish water (5–30 ppt), never in fresh water.
Alone, 24–29 °C, hard alkaline water. Counts 2.5 fish in the stocking.
Eats snails, shrimp and small fish and needs snails or hard food (shell food) for its teeth. Nips fins.
Does not breed in a tank.
Catch: aquarium net in mangrove swamps, wandering trader (rare).
info.bettacraft.tankmate.guppy:
Guppy (Poecilia reticulata) from Venezuela and Trinidad, today wild in warm waters worldwide.
Males with big colourful tails, females bigger and grey. Male bettas go for male guppies.
Shoal of 3 or more, 22–28 °C, water: hardy. Counts 0.35 fish in the stocking.
Bears live young.
Genetics: every guppy has its own genes for the tail shape (delta, triangle, swords, lyre, spade, round, flag), the body colour (gold, albino, blond, blue, black), the tail colour and pattern, and patterns on the X and Y chromosome (cobra, tuxedo, moscow, japan blue, red tail, red head): the Y patterns go only from the father to the sons. Females are grey but carry the genes. Named strains: Red Cobra, Blue Moscow, Full Gold, Tuxedo Koi and more. Crosses with endlers (hybrids).
Catch: aquarium net in rivers, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.harlequin_rasbo:
Harlequin Rasbora (Trigonostigma heteromorpha) from the peat swamps of Malaysia, Sumatra and Borneo.
Copper body with a black wedge; spawns upside down under broad leaves.
Shoal of 6 or more, 22–28 °C, water: sensitive. Counts 0.45 fish in the stocking.
Scatters its eggs (fine plants, spawning mop).
Catch: aquarium net in swamps, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.honey_gourami:
Honey Gourami (Trichogaster chuna) from the ponds and slow rivers of India and Bangladesh.
The male honey-orange with a dark blue-black throat and a yellow dorsal fin, the female beige with a brown stripe; bred as Gold and Red.
A pair or a small group, 22–28 °C, water: average. Counts 0.6 fish in the stocking.
A labyrinth fish that breathes air at the surface; peaceful, the calmest gourami. The male builds a foam nest and guards it.
Catch: aquarium net in swamps and rivers, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.honeycomb_moray:
Honeycomb moray (Gymnothorax favagineus) of the Indo-Pacific reefs: a big moray eel with dark spots in a pale network; 1.2 m in the game.
Big animal: needs a sea water tank of at least 15 × 8 × 4 blocks and 173 water blocks each; lives in a lair under the decoration (build it a rock cave), breathes with its mouth open and comes out at night and for food.
24–28 °C. Swallows fish, bettas and shrimp. Does not breed in a tank.
Catch: large net or steel leader in warm oceans (into a transport tub); rarely wild there.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.kuhli_loach:
Kuhli Loach (Pangio kuhlii) from the peat swamps of Indonesia and Malaysia.
An eel-like banded loach that rests in hiding by day and roams the bottom at night.
Shoal of 5 or more, 24–30 °C, water: sensitive. Counts 0.4 fish in the stocking.
Scatters its eggs (fine plants, spawning mop).
Catch: aquarium net in swamps, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.leopard_frog_pl:
L134 Leopard Frog Pleco (Peckoltia compta (L134)) from the Rio Tapajós in Brazil.
A small pleco with yellow and black bands. Lives in caves and on the glass, eats algae a little and needs warm water.
Fine on its own, 25–30 °C, water: sensitive. Counts 1 fish in the stocking.
Spawns in a cave, the male guards.
Catch: aquarium net in jungle water, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.lined_seahorse:
Lined Seahorse (Hippocampus erectus) from sea grass, mangrove roots and estuaries of the western Atlantic; the most common captive-bred seahorse.
Swims slowly and upright and holds on to plants, corals or decoration with its tail most of the time: needs hitching posts and low flow (no strong pumps).
Eats only live food: artemia nauplii and mosquito larvae, twice a day; slow next to fast fish. No tangs, damselfish, chromis or clownfish.
18–27 °C, sea water and strong brackish water (20–42 ‰). Counts 1.5 fish in the stocking.
The female lays her eggs into the brood pouch of the male, who gives birth to the fry a few days later; they eat artemia from the start.
Catch: aquarium net in lukewarm and warm oceans, wandering trader (rare).
info.bettacraft.tankmate.mosquito_rasbor:
Mosquito Rasbora (Boraras brigittae) from the blackwater peat swamps of Borneo.
One of the smallest aquarium fish (about 2 cm), red with a dark line. Also sold as chili rasbora - it is the same species.
Shoal of 8 or more, 22–28 °C, water: sensitive. Counts 0.12 fish in the stocking.
Scatters its eggs (fine plants, spawning mop).
Catch: aquarium net in swamps, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.motoro_stingray:
Motoro stingray (Potamotrygon motoro), the freshwater stingray of the Amazon: a round, flat disc with orange, black-ringed eye spots; 0.6 m with the tail.
Big animal: needs a tank of at least 8 × 4 × 2 blocks and 22 water blocks each; glides low over the ground with a ripple along its disc and lies on the substrate (sand) for long.
24–30 °C, soft, very clean water. Eats worms, shrimp and small bottom fish.
Livebearing: a pair has 2–5 pups after a long pregnancy, only as many as the tank has room for (size rule).
Catch: large net or steel leader in jungle water (into a transport tub); rarely wild there.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.neon_dwarf_rain:
Neon Dwarf Rainbowfish (Melanotaenia praecox) from the rivers of western New Guinea.
A deep body with shining neon-blue scales; the male has red fins, the female yellowish ones.
In a shoal of 6 or more, 23–28 °C, water: average. Counts 0.6 fish in the stocking.
Active and peaceful, two dorsal fins. Spawns into moss or a spawning mop.
Catch: aquarium net in jungle water and rivers, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.neon_tetra:
Neon Tetra (Paracheirodon innesi) from the blackwater streams of the upper Amazon (Peru, Colombia).
A blue neon stripe over a red rear half: the classic shoal fish.
Shoal of 6 or more, 20–27 °C, water: sensitive. Counts 0.35 fish in the stocking.
Scatters its eggs (fine plants, spawning mop).
Catch: aquarium net in jungle water, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.ocellaris_clown:
Ocellaris Clownfish (Amphiprion ocellaris) from the coral reefs of the eastern Indian Ocean and the western Pacific.
Orange with three white bands edged in black; lives in its host anemone (bubble tip anemone).
A pair, 24–28 °C, sea water (28–40 ‰). Counts 1 fish in the stocking.
The pair spawns at the foot of its anemone, the male guards the eggs.
Catch: aquarium net in warm oceans, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.odessa_barb:
Odessa Barb (Pethia padamya) from the rivers of Myanmar.
Silver-olive with black-edged scales; the male has a broad scarlet band along the side, the female two dark spots.
In a shoal of 6 or more, 18–26 °C (cooler than a betta tank), water: hardy. Counts 0.55 fish in the stocking.
Peaceful. Egg scatterer: many eggs into fine plants, moss or a spawning mop.
Catch: aquarium net in rivers, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.otocinclus:
Otocinclus (Otocinclus vittatus) from plant-rich streams of South America.
A tiny sucker catfish that grazes the glass and the leaves clean, in a small group.
Shoal of 5 or more, 21–27 °C, water: very sensitive. Counts 0.3 fish in the stocking.
Glues its eggs to the glass (after a cool water change).
Catch: aquarium net in jungle water, rivers, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.panda_cory:
Panda Cory (Corydoras panda) from cool clear streams of the Rio Ucayali in Peru.
Cream with a black eye mask, black dorsal fin and a spot at the tail base. Likes it cool.
Shoal of 6 or more, 20–26 °C, water: sensitive. Counts 0.45 fish in the stocking.
Glues its eggs to the glass (after a cool water change).
Catch: aquarium net in jungle water, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.pangasius:
Pangasius (Pangasianodon hypophthalmus), the iridescent shark catfish of the Mekong: a restless, silvery giant of big rivers, in a home tank about 1 m long.
Big animal: needs a tank of at least 12 × 6 × 3 blocks and 100 water blocks each; swims wide curves.
22–30 °C, eats everything and, once grown, small fish, young bettas and shrimp. Does not breed in a tank.
Catch: large net or steel leader in rivers and jungle water (into a transport tub); rarely wild in deep rivers.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.pearl_gourami:
Pearl Gourami (Trichopodus leerii) from the swamps of Thailand, Malaysia and Indonesia.
Covered with pearly dots, a dark line from the snout to the tail; the male has an orange-red throat and long fins.
A pair, 24–30 °C, water: average. Counts 1.6 fish in the stocking.
A labyrinth fish; the males claim territories and male bettas go for them. The male builds a big foam nest and guards it.
Catch: aquarium net in swamps and jungle water, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.platy:
Platy (Xiphophorus maculatus) from Mexico and Central America.
A sturdy, peaceful livebearer in many colours.
Shoal of 3 or more, 20–27 °C, water: hardy. Counts 0.5 fish in the stocking.
Bears live young.
Catch: aquarium net in rivers, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.pygmy_cory:
Pygmy Cory (Corydoras pygmaeus) from the Rio Madeira (Brazil).
A tiny cory that often hovers in a loose shoal in the middle of the water.
Shoal of 8 or more, 22–27 °C, water: sensitive. Counts 0.2 fish in the stocking.
Glues its eggs to the glass (after a cool water change).
Catch: aquarium net in jungle water, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.ram_cichlid:
Ram Cichlid (Mikrogeophagus ramirezi) from the llanos rivers of Venezuela and Colombia.
A small, colourful dwarf cichlid: golden head with a black bar through the eye, blue spangles; the female has a pink belly. Gold, Electric Blue and the short Balloon form.
As a pair, 25–31 °C, soft water, water: sensitive. Counts 0.8 fish in the stocking.
Open brooder: the pair cleans a flat stone and guards eggs and young. Fine with a betta if the tank is big enough.
Catch: aquarium net in rivers and jungle water, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.red_eye_puffer:
Red-Eye Puffer (Carinotetraodon irrubesco) from the blackwater of Sumatra and Borneo.
Brown with red eyes; the male has a dark belly edged white, a red keel and red fin edges, the female is spotted.
Alone or a species group without bettas, 23–29 °C, soft water, water: sensitive. Counts 0.5 fish in the stocking.
Eats snails and needs them or hard food (shell food) for its teeth. Nips fins.
Egg scatterer: lays its eggs into moss and fine plants.
Catch: aquarium net in swamps and jungle water, wandering trader (rare).
info.bettacraft.tankmate.redtail_catfish:
Redtail catfish (Phractocephalus hemioliopterus) of the Amazon and the Orinoco: a heavy catfish with a broad, flat head, long barbels, a white flank band and a bright red tail; 1.2 m in the game.
Big animal: needs a tank of at least 15 × 8 × 4 blocks and 173 water blocks each; rests on the ground by day.
20–28 °C, soft to medium water. A predator: swallows every small fish, betta and shrimp it can reach. Does not breed in a tank.
Catch: large net or steel leader in jungle water (into a transport tub); rarely wild there.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.reticulated_loa:
Reticulated Loach (Botia lohachata) from the rivers of northern India, Nepal and Bangladesh.
Grey-cream with a dark net of Y-shaped bands; gets about 10 cm long.
In a group of 5 or more, 24–30 °C, water: average. Counts 1.5 fish in the stocking.
Eats snails; busy and a bit rough at feeding time. Does not breed in a tank.
Catch: aquarium net in rivers and swamps, wandering trader (rare).
info.bettacraft.tankmate.rummy_nose_tetr:
Rummy-Nose Tetra (Hemigrammus rhodostomus) from the blackwater of the lower Amazon.
Silver with a bright red head and a tail striped black and white; the red fades in bad water.
In a tight shoal of 8 or more, 24–29 °C, soft water, water: sensitive. Counts 0.4 fish in the stocking.
Egg scatterer: eggs into fine plants, moss or a spawning mop.
Catch: aquarium net in jungle water, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.spotted_eagle_r:
Spotted eagle ray (Aetobatus ocellatus) of the warm seas: a dark ray with white spots, pointed wings, a duck-bill snout and a long whip tail; 1.5 m long in the game.
Big animal: needs a sea water tank of at least 18 × 9 × 5 blocks and 338 water blocks each; flies through open water with slow wing beats.
24–29 °C. Cracks clams and snails, eats shrimp. Does not breed in a tank.
Catch: large net or steel leader in warm oceans (into a transport tub); very rarely wild there.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.sterbai_cory:
Sterbai Cory (Corydoras sterbai) from the Rio Guaporé (Brazil, Bolivia), warm water.
Dark with white dots and orange pectoral fins; one of the few corys for warm betta tanks.
Shoal of 6 or more, 24–30 °C, water: average. Counts 0.6 fish in the stocking.
Glues its eggs to the glass (after a cool water change).
Catch: aquarium net in jungle water, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.swordtail:
Swordtail (Xiphophorus hellerii) from the rivers of Mexico and Central America.
Olive-green with a red zigzag line along the side; the male carries a long yellow "sword" edged black on the tail. Bred as Red and Red Wagtail (red with black fins).
In a group of 3 or more, 22–28 °C, hard water, water: hardy. Counts 0.8 fish in the stocking.
Livebearer: bears live young; a breeding box saves them from the adults.
Catch: aquarium net in rivers, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.tiger_barb:
Tiger Barb (Puntigrus tetrazona) from the rivers and swamps of Sumatra and Borneo.
Golden with four black bars and red fin edges; bred as Green (moss green) and Albino.
In a shoal of 6 or more, 20–28 °C, water: hardy. Counts 0.6 fish in the stocking.
A fin nipper: goes for bettas, angelfish, gouramis and male guppies, much more in a small shoal. Not with bettas.
Egg scatterer: many eggs into fine plants, moss or a spawning mop.
Catch: aquarium net in rivers and swamps, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.wels_catfish:
Wels catfish (Silurus glanis), the giant catfish of the deep rivers of Europe: a long, marbled body with an endless anal fin and two long barbels; 1.5 m in the game (wild up to 2.7 m).
Big animal: needs a tank of at least 18 × 9 × 5 blocks and 338 water blocks each; a night hunter that lies on the ground by day.
4–26 °C (no heater needed), hardy, neutral to hard water. Eats small fish, bettas and shrimp. Does not breed in a tank.
Catch: large net or steel leader in rivers (into a transport tub); very rarely wild in deep rivers.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.yellow_tang:
Yellow Tang (Zebrasoma flavescens) from the reefs of Hawaii.
A bright yellow disc with a white scalpel at the tail; grazes algae all day.
Alone, 24–28 °C, sea water (28–40 ‰), clean water. Counts 2.5 fish in the stocking.
Does not breed in a tank.
Catch: aquarium net in warm oceans, wandering trader (rare).
info.bettacraft.tankmate.yellow_watchman:
Yellow Watchman Goby (Cryptocentrus cinctus) from the sandy lagoons of the western Pacific.
Yellow with small blue spots; sits on the bottom and watches.
Alone, 22–28 °C, sea water (28–40 ‰). Counts 0.6 fish in the stocking.
Does not breed in a tank.
Catch: aquarium net in warm and lukewarm oceans, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.yellowtail_dams:
Yellowtail Damsel (Chrysiptera parasema), a small damselfish of the western Pacific.
Electric blue with a yellow tail; hardy, a good first reef fish.
Alone or a few, 23–28 °C, sea water (20–42 ‰). Counts 0.45 fish in the stocking.
Does not breed in a tank.
Catch: aquarium net in warm and lukewarm oceans, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.zebra_danio:
Zebra Danio (Danio rerio) from the rivers and rice fields of India and Bangladesh.
Blue-black and silver-gold stripes from the gill to the tip of the tail; bred as Leopard (spotted) and Golden.
In a shoal of 6 or more, 18–27 °C (also unheated), water: hardy. Counts 0.4 fish in the stocking.
A fast swimmer at the surface. Egg scatterer: many eggs into fine plants, moss or a spawning mop.
Catch: aquarium net in rivers and swamps, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.zebra_pleco:
L046 Zebra Pleco (Hypancistrus zebra (L046)) from the rocky rapids of the Rio Xingu in Brazil (protected in the wild).
Black and white stripes, very warm, clean water and a cave. Eats meaty food, not algae.
Fine on its own, 26–31 °C, water: very sensitive. Counts 0.9 fish in the stocking.
Spawns in a cave, the male guards.
Catch: aquarium net in jungle water, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tds_meter:
Measures the TDS (total dissolved solids, ppm) of a tank and shows the hardness: soft, medium hard or hard.
Normal water has about 250 ppm, reverse osmosis water 0. Food and waste raise it, water changes bring it back.
Never wears out.
info.bettacraft.trace_canister: Trace element solution for the dosing pump. Fresh sea water has some; they are used up within days. Above fresh sea water's level the corals show their strong colours.
info.bettacraft.transport_tub: Transport tub for one big animal. It is heavy: you walk slower while you carry a full one. Right-click a big enough tank to put the animal in (size rule: about 12 × 6 × 3 blocks per metre of the animal), open water to release it. Take big animals out of a tank in the tank menu.
info.bettacraft.tubifex:
Tubifex worms: live food with a strong conditioning value; a breeding pair fed with them stays in the mood twice as long.
Mining mud in a swamp sometimes drops a few: put them into a tubifex dish to start a culture.
Worms from a stale dish are of poor quality and may make the fish sick.
info.bettacraft.tubifex_dish:
Breeds tubifex worms. Right-click with mud, a bucket of water and some tubifex to start; feed it mulm, or let a pipe bring in the waste water of a tank.
The water goes stale and evaporates: a bucket of water on a full dish (or clean water from a pipe) rinses it. Harvest with the aquarium net; hoppers take the worms out too.
Right-click with an empty hand shows the state.
info.bettacraft.vallisneria:
Long ribbon leaves up to the surface; spreads quickly by runners.
Plant it in a tank interior on substrate; grows up to the water surface. From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 2.5 days to full size with medium light, nutrients (waste in the water) and 20-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.
Find it: the aquarium net in rivers, rarely fishing in rivers, the wandering trader; cuttings from trimming.
Shears: trim it (cuttings), inside or from outside on the tank where you look. Break the root: take the whole plant out. Full-grown it sends out runners.
info.bettacraft.water_change_controller: Next to a tank: changes a share of the water at an interval (screen: every 1 to 60 days, 5 to 50 %). The old water goes down the drain, fresh water comes from a reservoir, pipe or water source next to it.
info.bettacraft.water_lettuce:
Water lettuce (Pistia stratiotes): rosettes of velvety, ribbed leaves standing up like a cup, with long feathery roots; takes up much waste. Use it on a tank: it floats where you look at the water.
Grows with light and nutrients, forms offshoots and takes up waste.
Find it: fishing in swamps and mangrove swamps.
Take plants out: right-click the surface with an empty hand or an aquarium net; net + sneak thins the whole tank out by half.
info.bettacraft.water_pump:
Pulls water from the block behind it and pushes it into the block in front of it (200 mB/t). Place it looking where the water should go.
Right-click or sneak + mouse wheel: power regulator. Redstone stops it. With pipes.pumpsRequireEnergy it needs FE.
info.bettacraft.wild_coral:
A coral colony from a warm ocean reef.
Shears cut a frag off it for a reef tank; the colony grows back after a while.
It lives under water only; broken it drops nothing (silk touch: itself).
info.bettacraft.yeast:
Baker's yeast for the bio CO2 bottle: brown mushrooms and sugar set up in a bowl.
One yeast starts one brew.
info.bettacraft.zoanthus:
Soft coral: a carpet of polyps with orange discs that spreads over the rock.
Glue the frag onto reef rock in a reef tank. Light: medium, flow: gentle, no calcium.
Frag it with shears; wild colonies grow on the warm ocean reefs (shears cut frags off them), more frags from the aquarium net on a reef, vanilla corals or the wandering trader.

quest.bettacraft.big_tank.desc: Build a tank of at least 64 blocks. Big tanks hold sharks, rays and food fish.
quest.bettacraft.big_tank.title: Public Aquarium
quest.bettacraft.catch_betta.desc: Wild bettas live in swamps. Catch one with a water bucket or a fish bag.
quest.bettacraft.catch_betta.title: Labyrinth Fish
quest.bettacraft.chapter.subtitle: From the first tank to the reef and the terrarium
quest.bettacraft.chapter.title: Bettacraft
quest.bettacraft.co2.desc: Plants need CO2: a bio CO2 bottle with yeast beside the tank makes them grow faster, a CO2 cylinder even more. Too much CO2 harms the fish, so watch the values.
quest.bettacraft.co2.title: Fizz
quest.bettacraft.corals.desc: Corals grow on rock in a reef tank. Green star polyps are an easy start.
quest.bettacraft.corals.title: Polyps
quest.bettacraft.dosing.desc: Stony corals use calcium and carbonate. A dosing pump keeps the reef values steady.
quest.bettacraft.dosing.title: Reef Chemistry
quest.bettacraft.dynasty.desc: Raise a betta of the fifth generation.
quest.bettacraft.dynasty.title: Dynasty
quest.bettacraft.equipment.desc: A heater keeps the water warm, a filter keeps it clean and a light lets plants grow and shows the day. Put them on the outside of the glass.
quest.bettacraft.equipment.title: The Basics
quest.bettacraft.external_filter.desc: An external filter with good media keeps even a crowded tank clean.
quest.bettacraft.external_filter.title: Plumbing
quest.bettacraft.feeder.desc: An automatic feeder on the tank feeds the fish while you are away.
quest.bettacraft.feeder.title: Room Service
quest.bettacraft.fill_tank.desc: Fill the tank at least halfway with water buckets or pipes. Animals only go into a tank with enough water.
quest.bettacraft.fill_tank.title: Water Works
quest.bettacraft.first_tank.desc: Place tank blocks: one block is a small aquarium, blocks next to or on top of each other join into a bigger one, in any connected shape. The Bettacraft handbook explains everything step by step.
quest.bettacraft.first_tank.title: Glass House
quest.bettacraft.food_maker.desc: The food maker turns fish, grain and kelp into betta pellets by the dozen. Wind it up, or power it.
quest.bettacraft.food_maker.title: Food Factory
quest.bettacraft.fry_food.desc: The fry are tiny: culture infusoria or hatch artemia nauplii for them.
quest.bettacraft.fry_food.title: Microscopic Menu
quest.bettacraft.fry_free.desc: Raise the larvae until the fry swim free. Remove the father in time.
quest.bettacraft.fry_free.title: Free Swimming
quest.bettacraft.gecko.desc: Move a leopard gecko into a warm, dry terrarium.
quest.bettacraft.gecko.title: Leopard Gecko
quest.bettacraft.grown_up.desc: Raise a tank-bred betta to adulthood.
quest.bettacraft.grown_up.title: All Grown Up
quest.bettacraft.insert_betta.desc: Right-click the tank with the betta to put it in. Two adult males in one tank will fight!
quest.bettacraft.insert_betta.title: Moving In
quest.bettacraft.interior.desc: Sneak and right-click a tank to step into its interior, a world of its own at 16 blocks per tank block.
quest.bettacraft.interior.title: Honey, I Shrunk Myself
quest.bettacraft.monitor.desc: Monitors show the values of the tanks around them. An alarm tile warns you, with a redstone signal and a waypoint on the map.
quest.bettacraft.monitor.title: Control Room
quest.bettacraft.nest.desc: A healthy, well-fed male in warm, calm water builds a bubble nest. Floating plants help.
quest.bettacraft.nest.title: Bubble Architect
quest.bettacraft.pellets.desc: Craft betta pellets and feed by right-clicking the tank. The tank menu shows who is hungry.
quest.bettacraft.pellets.title: Fish Flakes
quest.bettacraft.plants.desc: Plant aquarium plants in the substrate. Plants take up waste and give the fish cover.
quest.bettacraft.plants.title: Green Thumb
quest.bettacraft.reverse_osmosis.desc: The reverse osmosis unit makes soft water for demanding fish, shrimp and the reef.
quest.bettacraft.reverse_osmosis.title: Pure Water
quest.bettacraft.sea_water.desc: Mix sea salt into reverse osmosis water, or bring sea water from the ocean, for a reef tank.
quest.bettacraft.sea_water.title: Salt Water
quest.bettacraft.skimmer.desc: A protein skimmer and live rock keep salt water clean.
quest.bettacraft.skimmer.title: Clean Reef
quest.bettacraft.spawned.desc: Put a ready female in with him: the pair spawns into the nest. Take her out afterwards.
quest.bettacraft.spawned.title: Clutch
quest.bettacraft.substrate.desc: Lay substrate on the interior floor: sneak and right-click it with sand, gravel or soil.
quest.bettacraft.substrate.title: Groundwork
quest.bettacraft.terrarium.desc: Every tank can be a terrarium or paludarium: build land above the water line in its interior, or leave the water out. Land animals travel in a terrarium box.
quest.bettacraft.terrarium.title: Dry Land
quest.bettacraft.terrarium_gear.desc: A basking lamp gives warmth and UV, a mister humidity, and the thermo-hygrometer shows both.
quest.bettacraft.terrarium_gear.title: Desert and Rainforest
quest.bettacraft.test_kits.desc: The pH test kit and the TDS meter show the water values. Bettas like soft, slightly acid water.
quest.bettacraft.test_kits.title: Test Your Water
quest.bettacraft.tropical.desc: Keep a tank with bettas at 26 to 28 °C. The tank menu shows the temperature.
quest.bettacraft.tropical.title: Tropical
quest.bettacraft.variety.desc: Breed a named variety such as Koi Galaxy, Samurai or Nemo. The magnifier shows the genes.
quest.bettacraft.variety.title: Designer Fish
quest.bettacraft.water_change.desc: Waste builds up in every tank. Pour fresh water into a tank with used water to change it.
quest.bettacraft.water_change.title: Fresh Start

sound_test.bettacraft.tank_drain: water scooped out of a tank

tankmate.bettacraft.breeding.cave: Spawns in a cave, the male guards
tankmate.bettacraft.breeding.cichlid_cav: Cave brooder: the female spawns in a small cave and guards the brood

tankmate.bettacraft.breeding.none: Does not breed in a tank

tankmate.bettacraft.breeding.pouch: Brood pouch: the male carries the eggs
tankmate.bettacraft.breeding.scatter: Scatters its eggs (fine plants, spawning mop)
tooltip.bettacraft.air_stone.usage: Place in a tank interior; an air pump next to the tank makes it bubble
tooltip.bettacraft.alder_cone: Right-click a tank: a few tannins; or lay it on the floor
tooltip.bettacraft.algae_scraper: Right-click the glass of a tank: cleans that glass face
tooltip.bettacraft.almond_leaf: Right-click a tank: tannins lower the pH a little and fade; or lay it on the floor
tooltip.bettacraft.amazon_frogbit: Round leaves with long roots: the favourite nest site
tooltip.bettacraft.artemia_cysts: One jar, one culture: craft it with a bottle of salt water or put it in an artemia hatchery.

tooltip.bettacraft.breeding_box.usage: Right-click a tank; take it out in the menu (breeding tab)
tooltip.bettacraft.bulkhead.usage: Use on a floor block of a tank: its connection appears on the interior floor
tooltip.bettacraft.cabinet: Put a tank on it. Holds an external filter and nine stacks; the feeder takes food from it.
tooltip.bettacraft.calcium_additive: Right-click a reef tank: more calcium for the stony corals
tooltip.bettacraft.co2_cylinder.solenoid: With solenoid valve: closes while the lights are off
tooltip.bettacraft.cooler.usage: Place it inside the tank interior (cools while under water) or put it into an external filter
tooltip.bettacraft.corner_filter.usage: Place in a tank interior (a corner suits it); a motor filter
tooltip.bettacraft.crank: Right-click a device with a spring to wind it; hold the button to keep winding
tooltip.bettacraft.culture: Ready after %s in-game day(s) (keep it in your inventory or a chest)
tooltip.bettacraft.culture.light: Ready after %s in-game day(s), needs light to hatch

tooltip.bettacraft.decor_coconut_cave: A small cave for small fish
tooltip.bettacraft.decor_diver_helmet: Small fish swim in through the face window

tooltip.bettacraft.decor_lava_rock: Porous rock with a small cave; young shrimp hide in it
tooltip.bettacraft.decor_mangrove_root: Wood: lowers the pH a little like driftwood
tooltip.bettacraft.decor_rowing_boat: Keel up on the bottom: a low cave for catfish
tooltip.bettacraft.decor_seiryu_stone: Grey rocks with calcite veins: they harden the water a little
tooltip.bettacraft.decor_ship_bow: The clay pipe in its hold is a spawning cave for plecos
tooltip.bettacraft.decor_shrimp_tubes: Young shrimp hide in the tubes
tooltip.bettacraft.decor_slate_cave: Stacked slate plates with a cave for catfish
tooltip.bettacraft.decor_spiderwood: Fine branches; wood lowers the pH a little
tooltip.bettacraft.decor_treasure_chest: Bubbles rise from the coins while an air pump runs
tooltip.bettacraft.dosing_canister.empty: Empty: fill it in the crafting grid
tooltip.bettacraft.external_filter.usage: Place it next to a tank or into a cabinet under the tank. Cleans the water, holds two heaters or coolers.
tooltip.bettacraft.fish_bag.empty: Right-click a small fish to catch it. Holds the fish and 100 mB of water.
tooltip.bettacraft.floating_plant: Use on a tank: floats on the water surface
tooltip.bettacraft.flow_pump.usage: Place it inside the tank interior; the outlet faces away from you
tooltip.bettacraft.heater.usage: Place it inside the tank interior (heats while under water) or put it into an external filter
tooltip.bettacraft.hornwort: Free-floating shoots deep into the water
tooltip.bettacraft.intake_sponge.usage: Use on a motor filter: it no longer sucks in fry
tooltip.bettacraft.interior_plumbing.usa: Place in a tank interior; joins the bulkhead's connection
tooltip.bettacraft.internal_filter.usage: Place it inside the tank interior; the outlet with the water jet faces you
tooltip.bettacraft.large_net: Catches a big animal (giant catfish, shark, ray, dolphin) into an empty transport tub in your inventory; swung in open water it now and then brings one up
tooltip.bettacraft.liquid_fertilizer.use: Right-click a tank: one portion into the water
tooltip.bettacraft.live_food.poor: From a foul dish: may make the fish sick
tooltip.bettacraft.magnifier: Right-click a tank: analyses the hidden genes of every animal in it
tooltip.bettacraft.magnifier.free: On this server every animal shows its genes anyway
tooltip.bettacraft.magnifier.menu: Tank menu: "Analyse" for one selected animal
tooltip.bettacraft.media.carbon: Chemical: clears the water; used up after a while
tooltip.bettacraft.media.ceramic: Biological: home of the bacteria, cleans the most; clogs slowly (wash it in a water cauldron)
tooltip.bettacraft.media.peat: Softens the water and lowers the pH; used up slowly
tooltip.bettacraft.media.sponge: Mechanical: holds back dirt; clogs fastest (wash it in a water cauldron)
tooltip.bettacraft.mirror_stick: Hold it up in front of a tank: male bettas that see it flare at their reflection
tooltip.bettacraft.mob_jar.empty: Right-click a mob weakened below %s %% of its health
tooltip.bettacraft.ph_test: Right-click a tank: pH and where it is drifting
tooltip.bettacraft.pour: Sneak + right-click (or into the air): pour out
tooltip.bettacraft.red_root_floater: Turns red under strong light, green under weak light
tooltip.bettacraft.remineraliser: Right-click a tank: raises the TDS (sneak: up to 150 ppm)
tooltip.bettacraft.ro_water_bucket: Pours plain water; into a tank a water change with nothing dissolved
tooltip.bettacraft.sea_salt: Right-click a tank: salts one bucket of its water to sea water (sneak: as much as it needs)
tooltip.bettacraft.sea_water_bucket: Salt water (35 ‰): fills a reef tank. Fill an empty bucket in an ocean or at a beach.
tooltip.bettacraft.sponge_filter.usage: Place in a tank interior; runs on an air pump, never sucks in fry
tooltip.bettacraft.steel_leader: Hold it in the other hand while fishing: now and then a big fish of the water bites (an empty transport tub in your inventory)
tooltip.bettacraft.tank: Aquarium block. Place several of the same glass next to each other to build a larger tank.
tooltip.bettacraft.tank.packed: Packed tank with %s animal(s): its water, interior and animals travel inside. Place it to set the tank up again.
tooltip.bettacraft.tank_net: Right-click a tank: takes out the floating plant or small animal you look at
tooltip.bettacraft.tank_net.sneak: Sneak + right-click: thins the tank out by half
tooltip.bettacraft.tank_net.water: In open water: catches shrimp, snails and frogs into an empty fish bag, now and then a plant from the bottom
tooltip.bettacraft.tankmate.clutch_hint: Right-click a tank (best one without adults) to raise them
tooltip.bettacraft.tds_meter: Right-click a tank: TDS (dissolved minerals) and hardness
tooltip.bettacraft.terrarium_box: Catches land animals: our tortoises, frogs, geckos and snakes, and the land animals of other mods with a terrarium profile
tooltip.bettacraft.terrarium_box.filled: Right-click a terrarium or paludarium to put it in, or the ground to let it go
tooltip.bettacraft.transport_tub: Carries one big animal. Right-click one in a tank (or take it out in the tank menu); wild ones need the large net
tooltip.bettacraft.transport_tub.filled: Heavy: you walk slower while you carry it. Right-click a big enough tank to put the animal in, or open water to release it
